content.text:
Fixed: `[foo *bar [baz](/url) qux*][ref]` now renders `

[foo bar baz qux]ref

`, matching CommonMark. The spec and unit tests pass (1832 pass, 0 fail). I didn't add a dedicated unit test; the fixed CommonMark spec case 533 covers it. **Cause:** Before parsing inline content, `inlineTokens` in `src/Lexer.ts` hides defined reference links from the emphasis matcher by replacing them with `[aaa…]`. It hid the whole outer `[foo *bar [baz](/url) qux*][ref]`, including the `*` delimiters inside it. A reference link whose text contains another link is then rejected as a link, so those delimiters were never matched and printed as plain text. **Fix:** I moved the masking into a new private method, `maskReflinks`, in `src/Lexer.ts`. When a reference link's text contains another link, it masks only the inner link and the trailing `[ref]` and leaves the outer text visible. If the text has no inner link, it masks the whole thing as before. **Other checks:** - `__` strong and an inner reference link (example 533) now work as well. - `*[a*][ref]` still behaves as before. **Spec change:** Example 533 was marked `"shouldFail": true` in `test/specs/commonmark/commonmark.0.31.2.json` and `test/specs/gfm/commonmark.0.31.2.json`. It now passes, so the test runner reported it as an unexpected pass. I removed that flag from both files.
